notes: Each governed fact has one stable factKey and exactly one authorityPath. Reports, plans, docs, and dashboards may project that authority but must not redefine it.
Governed facts have no fallback or double standard: implementations must consume the registered authority or remain projection-only with no acceptance power.
The mandatory functional-complete claim is always reduced through the registered reducer authority; report-local booleans are input evidence only.
Optional real-machine evidence may establish only the candidate-and-environment claim declared by the acceptance-standards authority and cannot change the functional-complete result.

authorities.domain: Product release version, tag, channel, package manifest set, container platforms, acceptance profile, GitHub runner matrix, and local verification engine.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Git tags, package manifests, lockfiles, workflow expressions, reports, and documentation are projections and cannot redefine the release.
The platform acceptance command catalog continues to own its command DAG; this definition selects a registered profile only.

authorities.domain: Immutable release source-candidate identity over the Git source revision and tree, release definition, package lock, canonical public package inventory, supported profile, and report-owner inventory.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: SOURCE_CANDIDATE.json is a write-once projection of this authority; jobs, reports, packages, images, signatures, plans, and receipts cannot recompute or replace its candidate digest.
Derived package, functional, and OCI authorities must bind the same candidate digest together with their own immutable artifact evidence.

authorities.domain: Mandatory functional-completeness release claim, optional real-machine verification claim, their one-way dependency, and the declared target set.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Workflow files, plans, reports, and documentation project the two standards but cannot redefine their dependency direction.
A real-machine receipt may establish only its candidate-and-environment support claim and cannot block or revoke functional-complete.

authorities.domain: Server operation definitions, generated operation registry projection, API capability projection, Operation Permission tool capability projection, and route/OpenAPI generated artifacts.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: tools/registry/operations/operations.registry.json and tools/registry/capabilities/capabilities.registry.json are generated projections and must not be edited as independent sources.
Generated operation, route, OpenAPI, and capability artifacts have no authority unless registry-validator parity and generator --check both pass.

authorities.domain: Process identity package issuance, signed request verification, rotation, revocation state, and server-signed revocation receipts.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: A client-submitted digest or status string is not a process identity revocation fact unless it verifies against server-signed and server-recorded process identity state.

authorities.domain: Final release readiness reduction across command failures, missing evidence, stale reports, leak scans, and delegated evidence reducers.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Generated report summary.releaseReady fields are reducer outputs or input evidence, never an independent release standard.
Aggregators must use createAggregateReleaseEvidenceReadiness() instead of rebuilding release readiness from local boolean expressions.

authorities.domain: Mandatory functional-completeness command DAG, acceptance layers, child report reduction, state transitions, and aggregate accepted-or-failed decision.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Child verifiers and report-local releaseReady fields provide input evidence only and cannot declare functional completeness.
The functional acceptance plan is a read-only projection and must not replace the aggregate acceptance report.
Real-machine verification is a downstream optional claim and cannot feed back into this authority.

authorities.domain: Canonical tag-triggered release publication, branch ancestry, serialized execution, immutable container version tags, signed flattened asset checksums, and release-note rendering.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: The built-in project release runbook prepares and validates candidates only; it cannot commit, tag, push, upload, publish, or bypass the workflow.
The MCP assembly-local SHA256SUMS is covered by the signed outer release checksum and is not an independent release authority.

authorities.domain: Private deployment open platform evidence command selection, required report derivation, and canonical scheduling.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: The private deployment verifier only reduces reports already produced by registered functional-completeness command owners.
The private deployment constants module owns only its aggregate report path and fixture scan constants; it does not own command execution, scheduling, or report membership.

authorities.domain: Authenticated upstream publishing, durable manifest publication, runtime snapshot replacement, Operation Permission revision, audience projection, and protocol delivery evidence.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: The server report terminates at server_published and depends only on the frozen wire contract observed through a neutral protocol peer.
Client repositories, builds, tests, caches, reports, receipts, and adoption state cannot block or promote this server fact.

authorities.domain: Immutable release tag, source commit and tree, complete upstream publishing report bundle, privacy scan, and the scoped upstream-publishing-prepublication-passed claim.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: The candidate receipt establishes only scoped upstream publishing prepublication evidence and never establishes or replaces the functional-complete release claim.
The HTML report is a human-readable candidate-context projection; only the external receipt binds the final HTML bytes and the complete artifact set.
Optional sibling services, plugins, clients, and their repositories do not become Meshrix Core release authorities.

authorities.domain: Self-contained upstream fixture transit evidence schema: REST and MCP registration, credential injection proof, projection parity, risk governance, and readiness reduction.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: A running fixture process or stale reports are not release evidence unless the reducer accepts the generated report.

authorities.domain: Upstream MCP gateway approval evidence: suspend-before-forward, approve-and-resume exactly once, rejection and expiry side-effect guards, audit correlation, and credential binding.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: A pending response alone is not approval-resume evidence; the reducer requires exactly one authenticated upstream fixture call after approval and no upstream calls after rejection, expiry, or repeated resolution.
Raw grants, pending operation ids, secret references, and credential material are not evidence; only reducer-accepted redacted proof fields may enter the report.

authorities.domain: Deterministic downstream agent tool loop evidence for every MCP release target: target-specific initialize, initialized notification, tools/list, tools/call, and denial turns through real meshrix-mcp proxy child processes over newline-delimited stdio JSON-RPC.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Downstream projection or direct fixture access is not proof that local client targets work unless this reducer accepts the spawned meshrix-mcp proxy newline-delimited stdio report.
Raw credential material is not evidence; only redacted hashes and reducer-accepted proof fields may enter release evidence.

authorities.domain: MCP downstream client real meshrix-mcp proxy newline-delimited stdio transport evidence and release-target profile coverage readiness.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Install/config discovery is not proof that the real meshrix-mcp proxy stdio transport works.
A direct HTTP MCP request is diagnostic only; release evidence must pass through the spawned proxy command and newline-delimited MCP stdio frames.

authorities.domain: Current downstream MCP release target names and membership.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Consumer-local hardcoded target arrays must not replace the shared target module.

authorities.domain: MCP process identity credential-store release evidence and platform backend readiness.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: File fallback or container-only proof cannot independently declare production credential-store readiness.

authorities.domain: Self-contained open source composition package root selection, copy plan, manifest hashing, and source package verification.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Generated manifests and package reports project the source package builder contract; they do not choose source roots or release package policy independently.

authorities.domain: Current Controlled Execution Convergence readiness reduction over exact Plan receipts, sandbox leaf reports, source provenance, privacy, Linux provider conformance, custody, and launcher-boundary evidence.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Sandbox leaf reports are reducer inputs and cannot independently claim current convergence readiness.

authorities.domain: npm script classification, tiers, side-effect policy, and CI profile metadata.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: package.json command strings define executable commands, but classification facts live only in tools/scripts/package-script-registry.ts.

authorities.domain: Open platform capability inventory, public functionality documentation mapping, requirement rows, and required integration edges.
nonAuthorityBoundaries: Capability docs may explain the surface, but release inclusion must trace back to the capability matrix and verifier reports.
